attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite name in the [set sprite position to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓Did you rename each sprite correctly? ❓Did you try out different x and y values to move your sprites’ positions?Sensei Pro Tip:💡 Remind ninjas that any block that refers to a sprite needs to come after its [set sprite to] block.
steps.instructions:
There are some code blocks in the [on start] container block already.


Rename the two sprites “cake” and “frog”. Position both sprites so they are not overlapping on the screen.


Update the name in the [set sprite image to] block, too.


Click ▶ to see the two sprites appear on the screen.

steps.hints:
❓Did you click ▶ then use the direction buttons to move your sprite around?


You can also use arrow or WASD keyboard keys to move your sprite:
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓ Did you drag the [move sprite with buttons] block inside the [on start] container block?❓ Did you drag the [set sprite stay in screen]  block inside the [on start] container block?

Sensei Pro Tip: 💡 Remind ninjas to select the correct sprite name in the new blocks.
steps.instructions:
Code the frog sprite to move with the direction buttons on the MakeCode game controller, and keep it from moving off the screen!


Click ▶  then use the on-screen direction buttons to move the frog sprite around the screen.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite kind in the [set sprite to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓ Which sprite needs its sprite kind updated?

Sensei Pro Tip:💡 Explain to ninjas that sprite kinds can be used to identify sprites and decide what events happen, and “food” is a generic category for something that the player is collecting or looking for.
steps.instructions:
Set the cake sprite as a new sprite kind. Sprite kinds can be used to identify sprites and decide what actions to take when events happen in the project. 


In the cake sprite’s [set sprite to] block, notice that the sprite kind is set to Player by default. Click the ⏷ on the sprite kind value to open the drop down menu, then select “Food” as the sprite kind.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add an [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block to an empty spot on the coding area?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓ Did you place the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block in a different spot in the coding area, instead of trying to place it inside or over the [on start] container block?❓ Why do you think the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container will be useful?Sensei Pro Tip:💡 Explain to ninjas that the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block can be placed anywhere on the coding area, as long as it does not block the other blocks already in the space.
steps.instructions:
Make something happen when the Player (frog) and Food (cake) sprites touch - or overlap - on screen!


Open the Sprites code block menu then drag out a [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block. Place the new container block anywhere in the coding area so that it does not block the code in the [on start] container block.


The [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block is a function that can be used to control what happens when sprites overlap.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite kind in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution: ﻿

Ask the ninja:❓ Which sprite kind should you update - the first or second? What should you update it to?❓What do you think will happen when the Player sprite overlaps with the Food sprite?

Sensei Pro Tip: 💡 The sprite kind information will be used instead of the sprite names in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block. Ninjas will see this in action in the following Level 4 activities.
steps.instructions:
Change the sprite kind in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block.


The first sprite kind will stay set to “Player”, but the second sprite kind should be changed to “Food”. Click the ⏷ on the second sprite kind value to open the drop down menu, then select “Food” as the sprite kind.


The sprite kind is a parameter that gives more information to the [on sprite overlaps sprite] function to customize what the code does.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you move the [set sprite image to] block inside the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓ Did the program work as expected? ❓ Are the correct sprite names and kinds selected in the code blocks?Sensei Pro Tip:💡 Remind ninjas that they should hold Ctrl on a PC or Command on a Mac as they click the block to select and move a single block.
steps.instructions:
Change the Food (cake) sprite image when the two sprites overlap!


From the [on start] container block, select the [set sprite image to] block and drag it into the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block. 


To select a single block from a chunk of code, press and hold Ctrl on a Windows computer or Command on a Mac as you click and drag out the block.


Click ▶ to see the Food (cake) sprite image change when it overlaps with the frog sprite!

steps.hints: ❓Did you drag a [sprite start effect] block inside the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓Did you explore the special effects and select one that you like?❓Did you change how long that effect happens for?

Sensei Pro Tip: 💡 Explain that some blocks have parameters, which is a piece of information that changes how a program runs.
steps.instructions:
Code the Player (frog) sprite to react when it reaches the cake sprite! Open the Sprites code block menu, drag a [sprite start effect] block into this project, then select the frog sprite and an effect. 


To control how long the effect lasts, click + to change the time parameter to make the effect longer or shorter.


Click ▶ to see what happens to the Player (frog) sprite when it overlaps with the cake sprite!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you drag the [set background image] and [play sound] code blocks inside the correct container blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:❓ Where should the background image block go to set the background at the beginning of the project?❓ Where should the sound block go to make the sound play when the sprites overlap?

Sensei Pro Tip:💡Remind ninjas that the sequence of code blocks will change how the project runs.  💡 Guide ninjas to notice that they may want to reposition their sprites’ starting positions depending on the background image they chose.
steps.instructions:
Customize this project with a background and sound. Drag a [set background image] block on top of the other blocks inside the [on start] container block to select or draw a background for this project.


Drag a [play sound] block into the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block to play a sound when the frog and cake sprites overlap on screen. Allow the sound to play [until done].


Click ▶ to see how these blocks changed this project!

subgroups.introduction: Learn how to make something happen when two sprites overlap!

validationItems.text: Change the 2 sprites’ names and sprite kinds
Move the Player sprite with the direction buttons and set it to stay in screen
Use an On Overlap block with sprite kinds Player and Food
Change the sprite image when sprites overlap
Use a sprite effect and change the effect parameters when sprites overlap
Play a sound when sprites overlap

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of White Belt! Before you create your final White Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn about functions, which are chunks of code that run whenever they are called. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Function Junction
badges.description: Use functions to make something happen at different points in a project.

badges.title: A Whole New Kind of Sprite
Making a Connection
badges.description: Make something happen when 2 different sprites overlap.

badges.title: Right Behind You
badges.description: Set one sprite to follow another sprite.

badges.title: Make It Dazzle
badges.description: Add an effect to any sprite.

badges.title: The End of the Road
badges.description: End the game in a win or loss when something happens in a project.
